title: Artificial intelligence in higher education: the state of the field
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper presents a PRISMA-based systematic review of artificial intelligence in higher education (HE) research published from 2016 through 2022. The authors sought to update earlier reviews and describe how the field has evolved, including where studies were conducted, which academic departments produced the research, which student populations were studied, and what AI was used for in HE settings. They also aimed to identify trends and gaps in the literature to inform future work.

The review screened 371 records and included 138 peer-reviewed journal articles. The studies covered 31 countries across six continents, with the largest share from Asia, especially China and Taiwan, and a substantial number from North America and Europe. Most studies focused on undergraduate students, though graduate students were also represented. First authors were most often affiliated with colleges of education, followed by computer science. The paper notes a strong increase in publications in 2021 and 2022, suggesting rapid growth in the field.

Using grounded coding, the authors found five main uses of AI in HE: assessment/evaluation, predicting, AI assistants, intelligent tutoring systems, and managing student learning. Across the review, AI was used for tasks such as automated assessment and feedback, performance and dropout prediction, chatbot or virtual-agent support, adaptive tutoring, and learning analytics for instructional decision-making. The authors conclude that AI is increasingly being used in traditional efficiency-enhancing ways, while more exploratory and pedagogically transformative uses remain underdeveloped. They call for more research in underrepresented regions, more work at the graduate level, more attention to instructors and managers, and exploration of newer tools such as ChatGPT.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI / AI assistant used for educational tasks such as answering questions, providing feedback, generating questions, and supporting instruction; the paper does not identify one specific commercial product.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is a systematic review of artificial intelligence in higher education from 2016-2022. It includes studies of AI assistants, intelligent tutoring systems, assessment/evaluation tools, predicting applications, and learning analytics, but does not isolate a single named generative AI product such as ChatGPT.

findings.finding_summary: Across 138 higher-education studies, the review found that AI was used mainly for assessment/evaluation, predicting, AI assistants, intelligent tutoring systems, and managing student learning. The paper does not report a single quantified effect for a named GenAI product; instead it synthesizes heterogeneous uses and notes that much of the evidence reflects traditional efficiency-oriented applications rather than unexplored affordances.
findings.measure: Systematic review synthesis of 138 peer-reviewed journal articles (AI use categories in higher education)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review with transparent PRISMA methods, but it synthesizes heterogeneous studies rather than testing one AI tool directly. The evidence is therefore descriptive and review-based, not a single high-causal-design intervention study.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports broad field trends and categories of AI use, but no direct effect sizes for a specific tool. Because no single intervention outcome is quantified, impact is unclear rather than demonstrably large or small.
